The estimated effect is about 0.65 log points, which rounds to **1**.

I treated this as a sharp regression discontinuity on the Tory candidates (223 observations), with `margin` as the running variable and winning (`margin > 0`) as the treatment. I fit separate linear regressions on each side of the cutoff and took the difference in predicted `ln.net` at a zero margin:

- Predicted ln.net at zero margin, winners: 13.19
- Predicted ln.net at zero margin, losers: 12.54
- Difference: 0.65 (SE about 0.29)

The result is robust to the specification. A common-slope model gives 0.60, and interacted models restricted to bandwidths of 0.1, 0.2 and 0.3 give 0.84, 0.60 and 0.72. Every variant rounds to 1. The estimate is not statistically significant at conventional levels.

ANSWER: 1
